messages:
sam: Heads-up 106 11 I'm flying to Tokyo for two weeks next month for customer meetings. Do I need anything special from benefits for medical visits there? Also my suitcase was delayed last trip so I'd rather get a physical ID card mailed to a friend9s US address and have them forward it. Is that allowed?
Jordan (People Ops): Short: download the digital card and get a travel "coverage verification" letter. Carriers usually don9t ship physical cards internationally, but mailing to a US address is possible (we can request). Details below.
Leah: I did this last year 10 digital card worked for the travel clinic, and the carrier told me to call their international assistance number before I saw anyone. They also recommended taking itemized receipts.
sam: Thanks 10 how do I request the coverage letter and how fast can you mail a physical card to my sister in CA?
Jordan (People Ops): To request a letter we need: member name, DOB, plan ID (on your portal), travel dates, and destination. We submit to the carrier; turnaround is usually 1-3 business days. For a physical card mailed to a US address we can change the mailing address temporarily but carriers vary12 some will only send to the member9s home address on file. If you provide your sister9s address we9ll check and request expedited mail. Expect 5-10 business days domestic if allowed.
sam: If I have to get a vaccine or visit a clinic and they9re out-of-network, will claims be covered? How do I avoid big OOP costs?
Jordan (People Ops): International care: most carriers treat international providers as out-of-network but will reimburse "emergency" or "medically necessary" care per your plan terms. Non-emergency routine care abroad is often OON and reimbursed at a lower rate. Steps to reduce OOP risk: 1) Call the carrier9s international assistance line before care for pre-certification when possible; 2) get an itemized bill and English translation if needed; 3) submit a claim with the itemized receipt + proof of payment; 4) ask the provider for a CPT/ICD code if available. We can also request a pre-authorization or a Letter of Medical Necessity if it's a planned procedure.
Benefits Bot: Need help? Digital ID: https://benefits.redwoodinc/id-card. Claim portal: https://benefits.redwoodinc/claims. International assistance: +1-800-555-0199 (Carrier Global Assist).
sam: HSA question: if I pay cash to a travel clinic in Japan, is that HSA-eligible? And do I need receipts in USD?
Jordan (People Ops): Yes, eligible medical expenses paid out-of-pocket are generally HSA-eligible. Keep itemized receipts showing service, date, provider, and amount. Convert the currency to USD (bank conversion rate or card statement) and include the conversion method when you file for reimbursement or HSA withdrawals. Save the original receipt.
sam: If a claim gets denied because the provider was OON, can we appeal? How long, and do you help?
Jordan (People Ops): You can appeal. Typical flow: submit appeal to carrier within 180 days (carrier-specific). We can help by providing Letter of Coverage or plan language and escalating to the carrier9s appeals team. Bring receipts, contemporaneous medical notes, and any pre-authorization docs. We9ll open a case with the carrier if you drop the claim reference here or email benefits@redwood.com.
Leah: FYI the carrier expedited a digital card/letter for me same day when I explained travel and an appointment. They gave a PDF proof of coverage you can print.
Benefits Bot: Request received: Travel verification request submitted. Reference TRV-2026-3378. You9ll get carrier PDF and membership confirmation by email once they process it.
sam: Awesome 10 sending plan ID and travel dates to benefits@redwood.com now. If the clinic needs the card immediately, I9ll show the digital card + the email from the carrier. Thanks!
